title: Cardinal Rental Reimbursement Extension Days and the Day Room of a Loss
content:
**Clause.** Under Cardinal Rental Reimbursement, the rental being extended is the claim's most recently entered authorization. The days authorized on it are its authorization plus every extension of it.

The **day room** of the loss is the option's maximum days per loss, less the days already used on the claim. The days already used are the days billed on every agency payment and every reimbursement on the claim, plus the days authorized on the rental being extended.

The **days the per-loss maximum can still pay** are worked out in three stages:
1. Take the option's per-loss maximum, less the agency and reimbursement payments on the claim net of agency credits.
2. From that, take away the days authorized on the rental being extended multiplied by the lower of its recorded daily rate and the option's daily limit. If the result is below zero, treat it as zero.
3. Divide by the daily limit and round down to a whole day.

The days an extension adds are the lowest of three figures: the option's extension increment, the day room, and the days the per-loss maximum can still pay. They are never fewer than zero.

## Worked computation (hypothetical claim on Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 40/1200: 30 maximum days, 5-day increment, $40.00 daily limit, $1200.00 per-loss maximum)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Agency payment on the claim | 10 days billed, $400.00 |
| Reimbursement on the claim | 3 days billed, $120.00 |
| Rental being extended | 7 days authorized, recorded rate $45.00 |
| Day room: 30 less (10 plus 3 plus 7) | 10 |
| Money left: $1200.00 less $520.00, less 7 multiplied by $40.00 | $400.00 |
| Days the per-loss maximum can still pay: $400.00 divided by $40.00 | 10 |
| Days the extension adds: the lowest of 5, 10 and 10 | 5 |

## Second illustration (hypothetical)

Same option, but $900.00 already paid on the claim and the same 7-day rental at $45.00. The money left is $1200.00 less $900.00 less $280.00, which is $20.00. $20.00 divided by $40.00 is 0.5, which rounds down to 0. The extension adds 0 days.
